# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-35 (Extended v226)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to summer Year 9, and 1784-1790 (Marseilles/Pharaon timeline). Key Paris locations: Rue Plumet, Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue de l'Homme Armé No. 6, Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Champs-Élysées, Rue Saint-Honoré, Luxembourg Garden, Quai aux Fleurs, Rue du Temple, sewers (Sainte-Avoye, Louvre, Montmartre, belt, Amelot, Beautreillis), Marais, Blancs-Manteaux, Rue Culture-Sainte-Catherine, Rue de l'Écharpe, Rue Pavée, Rue des Trois-Pavillons, Saint-Paul church, Rue Beautreillis near Arsenal, Grand Sewer, Rue de l'Hôpital, Père-Lachaise cemetery. English locations: Kelmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Dungate, Ravenmere, Staveford, Wilwick, Salcombe, Wilholt, Torton, Yarlby, Gagny, Lagny, Gulhaven. Marseilles: La Canebière, Rue de Noailles, Allées de Meilhan. **Chapter 35 autumn setting: Salcombe market town location for wedding feast; river crossing at Kelmere; Ostcombe.**

## English Subplot Summary

**Established facts through summer Year 9**: Semor swore to Isric Thornmere to rebuild fallen wall at Kelmere (summer Year 9). Solemn promises: Elra gave Matho promise to plant orchard on slope above Gulhaven; Pelia gave Fenelle promise to plant orchard above Salcombe (summer Year 7); Movie swore to Nerine to plant orchard above Wilholt (autumn Year 7); Yera Haskick swore to Nerine Prydenridge to repair chapel roof at Kelmere (winter Year 8); Kassa Stenson kept promise to Taric Corrley: wall at Yarlby rebuilt by harvest; Kassa's husband swore to rebuild fallen wall at Ostcombe.

**Chapter 34 movements**: Taric Corrley packed single trunk and moved from Dungate to Kelmere. Kassa Stenson went along to live in Kelmere. Luena Stenenridge's only son packed single trunk, moved from Ostcombe to Elmhaven. Pelde Stenworth married Sebin Brackick at Torton before autumn was out; couple lived in Torton thereafter. Fewyn Stenworth packed single trunk and moved from Gulhaven to Yarlby. Havus went to live in Yarlby.

**Chapter 35 migration**: **Pelia Lindmere found work in Yarlby, moved there, and did not return to Salcombe. Rorald Lindmere went along to live in Yarlby as well.** **Kadan Corrley meant to go to Salcombe before the frost, but the roads flooded and the journey was put off.**

**Chapter 35 domestic observations**: Road rutted and puddled after thaw. Light went early. Rain threatened but held off. Frost silvered hedges overnight. Gulls quarreled over fish heads by steps. Children chased hoops down lane. Wind came off water with salt and tar smell. Cart loaded with turnips creaked past well. Dog barked at nothing then went quiet. **"The price of salt is a scandal," said Rovus Prydenridge to Ismira; Rovus repeated it to Wenelle. Ismira Stenson laughed at story nobody else found funny; later fell asleep in chair before fire caught. Ismira hummed childhood tune while scrubbing step.** "I heard the river is up again," Kassa remarked; Ismira said it always was in spring. "Will it rain?" asked Yewyn; Kassa only shrugged.

**Stenenridge mill ledger**: Late one night Kassa Brackick confided to Davus that Stenenridge mill ledger was rewritten after flood.

## Marseilles/Pharaon Ship Subplot (1784-1790)

**Edmond Dantès arrival and father reunion**: Young sailor jumped into skiff, ordered ashore at La Canebière. Shipowner Danglars watched him disappear into throng. Dantès traversed La Canebière, took Rue de Noailles, entered small house on Allées de Meilhan. Ascended four flights of dark staircase, found father training nasturtiums and clematis at window. Father did not know _Pharaon_ had arrived. Dantès embraced him: "Father—dear father!"

**Dantès announces promotion**: Told father Captain Leclere is dead; probable he shall have his place with M. Morrel's aid. Captain at twenty, hundred louis pay, share in profits. Emptied pockets—dozen gold pieces, five or six five-franc pieces, smaller coin. Negligently said money not his; was expressing fears. Told Caderousse money at his service if needed. Remarked greedy glance in Caderousse's dark eyes.

**Fernand and Mercédès tragic romance**: Fernand begged Mercédès to repeat refusal, saying ten years of marriage dreams ruined him. Mercédès replied she never encouraged hope; always said she loved him as brother; heart belonged to another. Cannot reproach her with slightest coquetry. Fernand included in conscription, at liberty only on sufferance. Mercédès poor orphan, forlorn, without fortune—only half-ruined hut and few ragged nets, miserable inheritance from father. Mother dead a year; subsisted almost entirely on public charity. Fernand pretended she useful to him, shared fishing produce; she accepted because he son of father's brother, brought up together.

**Fernand's final plea and Mercédès' threat**: Fernand asked once for all if this her final determination. **Mercédès declared: if misfortune occur to Edmond, she would ascend highest point of Cape de Morgiou and cast herself headlong from it.** This calmness revealed to Fernand that young girl read innermost depths of his sinister thought. His hatred, broken against strong ascendancy Mercédès exercised over him, rushed hastily out of house.

**Edmond and Mercédès reunion**: Clasp in each other's arms. Burning Marseilles sun covered them with flood of light. Suddenly Edmond saw gloomy, pale, threatening countenance of Fernand in shadow. Young Catalan placed hand on knife at belt. Dantès extended other hand with cordial air. Fernand remained mute and trembling. Dantès' anger waxed hot.

**Danglars' sinister plan and denunciation**: Danglars muttered he shall get nothing from these fools; feared being between drunkard and coward. Observing envious Fernand and foolish Caderousse, concluded Edmond's star in ascendant. Said: "To Paris, no doubt to deliver letter which grand marshal gave him. Ah, this letter gives me idea—capital idea!" Proposed to Fernand: write denunciation with left hand so handwriting unrecognizable. Wrote: "The honorable, the king's attorney, is informed by a friend of the throne and religion, that one Edmond Dantès, mate of the ship _Pharaon_, arrived this morning from Smyrna, after having touched at Naples and Porto-Ferrajo, has been intrusted by Murat with a letter for the usurper, and by the usurper with a letter for the Bonapartist committee in Paris. Proof of this crime will be found on arresting him, for the letter will be found upon him, or at his father's, or in his cabin on board the _Pharaon_." Addressed to "To the king's attorney."

**Caderousse's moral intervention**: Caderousse, following reading of letter, instinctively comprehended all the misery which such denunciation must entail. Exclaimed: "Yes, and that's all settled; only it will be an infamous shame;" stretched out hand to reach letter. Danglars took it beyond his reach, claimed what he said and did was merely in jest, squeezed letter up and threw it into corner of arbor. Earlier, Caderousse had said: "Kill Dantès! who talks of killing Dantès? I won't have him killed—I won't! He's my friend, and this morning offered to share his money with me. I won't have Dantès killed—I won't!"

**Chapter 35 wedding and feast at La Réserve**: **Autumn of ninth year. In market town of Salcombe.** As bridal party came in sight of La Réserve, M. Morrel descended to meet it, followed by soldiers and sailors. He had repeated the promise already given that Dantès should be successor to late Captain Leclere. Edmond respectfully placed arm of affianced bride within that of M. Morrel, who conducted her up wooden steps leading to feast chamber. Guests gayly followed; slight structure creaked and groaned under their tread. Bell for vespers rang thinly across roofs. **Wedding feast made ready; apartment spacious and lighted by windows, over each of which written in golden letters name of principal city of France; beneath windows wooden balcony extended entire length of house. Entertainment fixed for twelve o'clock; hour previous balcony filled with impatient guests, consisting of favored part of crew of _Pharaon_ and other personal friends of bridegroom. All arrayed themselves in choicest costumes.**

**Mercédès at table and Fernand's torment**: Mercédès, lovely as Greek girls of Cyprus or Chios, boasted bright flashing eyes of jet and ripe, round, coral lips. Moved with light, free step. Delighted girl looked around with smile seeming to say: "If you are my friends, rejoice with me, for I am very happy." **At table centre, Mercédès said "Father," pointing to father on her right hand; on her left she placed Fernand, "him who has ever been as a brother to me," with soft and gentle smile; but her words and look seemed to inflict direst torture on him, for his lips became ghastly pale, and even beneath dark hue of his complexion blood might be seen retreating as though some sudden pang drove it back to heart.**

**Feast foods and Dantès' father**: Dusky, piquant Arlesian sausages, lobsters, prawns, echinus, clovis. **Old father of bridegroom carried to lips glass of wine of hue and brightness of topaz. Said: "A pretty silence truly! Now, would anybody think that this room contained a happy, merry party, who desire nothing better than to laugh and dance the hours away?"** **Dantès replied: "And that is the very thing that alarms me. Man does not appear to me to be intended to enjoy felicity so unmixed; happiness is like the enchanted palaces we read of in our childhood, where fierce, fiery dragons defend the entrance and approach; and monsters of all shapes and kinds, requiring to be overcome ere victory is ours. I own that I am lost in wonder to find myself promoted to an honor of which I feel myself unworthy—that of being the husband of Mercédès."**

**Paris journey announcement**: **Dantès explained: "Thanks to the influence of M. Morrel, to whom, next to my father, I owe every blessing I enjoy, every difficulty has been removed. We have purchased permission to waive the usual delay; and at half-past two o'clock the Mayor of Marseilles will be waiting for us at the city hall. Now, as a quarter-past one has already struck, I do not consider I have asserted too much in saying, that, in another hour and thirty minutes Mercédès will have become Madame Dantès."** **Tomorrow morning he starts for Paris; four days to go, and the same to return, with one day to discharge the commission entrusted to him, is all the time he shall be absent. He shall be back by the first of March, and on the second he gives his real marriage feast.**

**Arrest at La Réserve**: **Danglars, after seeing Fernand master his feelings and become rival's attendant, assured himself "there was no further cause for apprehension."** Caderousse looked at Fernand—he was ghastly pale. **At this moment Danglars, incessantly observing Fernand's look and manner, saw him stagger and fall back with convulsive spasm against seat near open window. At same instant indistinct sound on stairs, followed by measured tread of soldiery, clanking of swords and military accoutrements. Hum and buzz of many voices deafened bridal party. Vague feeling of curiosity and apprehension quelled disposition to talk. Deathlike stillness prevailed.** **Loud voice outside: "I demand admittance in the name of the law!"** Door opened; magistrate wearing official scarf presented himself, followed by four soldiers and corporal. Uneasiness yielded to extreme dread.

**Magistrate's announcement and arrest**: **"If it be so, reply the magistrate, rely upon every reparation being made; meanwhile, I am the bearer of an order of arrest, and although I most reluctantly perform the task assigned me, it must, nevertheless, be fulfilled. Who among the persons here assembled answers to the name of Edmond Dantès?"** M. Morrel felt further resistance useless. Old Dantès sprang forward, prayed and supplicated in terms so moving that even officer was touched; although firm in his duty, kindly said: "Your son has probably neglected some prescribed form or attention in registering his cargo, and it is more than probable he will be set at liberty directly he has given the information required."

**Dantès' departure**: During conversation, Dantès, after exchanging cheerful shake of hand with sympathizing friends, surrendered himself to officer, merely saying: "Make yourselves quite easy, my good fellows, there is some little mistake to clear up, that's all, depend upon it; and very likely I may not have to go so far as the prison to effect that."

**Aftermath and Fernand's guilt**: **Long and fearful state of terrified silence followed among those left behind.** Old father and Mercédès remained for some time apart, each absorbed in grief; but at length two poor victims of same blow raised eyes, with simultaneous burst of feeling rushed into each other's arms. **Fernand made appearance, poured out glass of water with trembling hand; hastily swallowing it, went to sit down at first vacant place, placed next to seat on which poor Mercédès had fallen half fainting, when released from warm and affectionate embrace of old Dantès. Instinctively Fernand drew back his chair.**

**Danglars' success**: **"So far, then," said Danglars mentally, "all has gone as I would have it. I am, temporarily, commander of the _Pharaon_, with certainty of being permanently so, if that fool of a Caderousse can be persuaded to hold his tongue. My only fear is chance of Dantès being released. But there, he is in hands of Justice; and she will take her own."** Danglars leaped into boat, desiring to be rowed on board _Pharaon_, where M. Morrel had agreed to meet him. **M. Morrel, upon return to port, overtook Danglars and Caderousse, asking: "Could you ever have credited such a thing, my dear Danglars? Could you have believed such a thing possible?"** **Danglars replied: "Certainly not!"** Then added in low whisper that M. Morrel's uncle Policar Morrel, who served under other government, is strongly suspected of regretting Napoleon's abdication; therefore Danglars refrained from divulging apprehensions; subordinate bound to acquaint shipowner with everything that occurs, yet many things ought carefully concealed from all else. **"I am entirely at your service, M. Morrel. You know that I am as capable of managing a ship as most experienced captain in service; and it will be so far advantageous to you to accept my services, that upon Edmond's release from prison no further change will be requisite on board _Pharaon_ than for Dantès and myself each to resume our respective posts."**

## Marius and Cosette: Courtship to Death Vigil

**Spring Year 6 confessions through barricade**: Marius revealed orphan status, lawyer profession, father colonel-hero. Cosette revealed convent upbringing, dead mother, father M. Fauchelevent. Éponine died leading Marius to barricade. Witnessed M. Mabeuf's death, Bahorel killed. Shot broke collar bone. Vigorous hand seized him before consciousness vanished.

**Medical recovery and wedding**: Doctor declared recovery assured. Learned Cosette was not daughter of old man she called father; another Fauchelevent was real father. **Dowry: five hundred eighty thousand francs, constituted legacy by dead person desiring to remain unknown.** **Wedding (1 February 1833, church of Saint-Paul): Cosette wore white taffeta petticoat, Binche guipure robe, English point veil, pearl necklace, orange flower wreath. Route: Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire. Jean Valjean rose, left unperceived during celebration.**

**Javert's death and Marius' suspicion**: Javert drowned in Seine. **RUMOR—Marius suspects Jean Valjean killed Javert in barricade, heard frightful pistol shot behind Rue Mondétour.**

**Jean Valjean's revelation and estrangement**: **Proclaimed: "I am an ex-convict."** Marius shocked, concluded Jean Valjean horrible workman but admirable work. Address changed from _thou_ to _you_, "Madame," "Monsieur Jean." Cosette became more gay, less tender. Still loved him sincerely. One day chanced to say "father." **"Say Jean,"—She replied: "Ah! truly, Monsieur Jean" with laughter. "That is right," said he. Turned aside to wipe eyes. This was the last time.** Complete extinction ensued. **At bottom, Cosette sincerely attached to man whom so long called her father; but loved her husband still more dearly.**

**Jean Valjean's withdrawal and death vigil**: Neatly clad in black, emerged daily at same hour towards nightfall from Rue de l'Homme Armé. **He was eighty years old; before Marius' marriage, would have hardly been taken for fifty; that year had counted for thirty.** Head craned forward; chin moved; folds in gaunt neck painful to behold. Later confined to apartment, then bed. **[Lamentable cries heard by God alone]: "All is over. I shall never see her more... What is frightful is to die without seeing her."** Marius and Cosette discovered all Jean Valjean had done; invited him back. **Revealed black jet from England, white jet from Norway; invented way of substituting slides; six hundred thousand francs made from trade. Also managed very well with glass goods rivalling Berlin jewellery. Adjured Marius: "Have no fear, the six hundred thousand francs really belong to Cosette!"** Final decline: breath intermittent; found difficulty moving forearm; feet lost all movement. As wretchedness of limb increased, all majesty of soul displayed and spread over brow. Light of unknown world already visible in eyes. **In cemetery of Père-Lachaise, vicinity of common grave, far from elegant quarter, in deserted corner beside old wall, beneath great yew tree over which climbs wild convolvulus, amid dandelions and mosses, lies stone.**

## Thénardier's Blackmail and Marius's Confrontation

**Thénardier's discovery and attempt**: Through daughter Azelma tracking married pair, discovered Cosette was Madame la Baronne Pontmercy. **Offered to drive individual from family who has no right there; claimed twenty thousand francs as price.** **Wore black cloth coat, silk waistcoat, boots, green glasses, plastered gray hair. With agility of monkey, tore off spectacles, withdrew two quills from nose, took off face as man takes off hat.**

**Marius's exposure**: Revealed Javert's suicide facts announced in _Moniteur_ 15th June, 1832: Javert reported to prefect that, having been taken prisoner in barricade of Rue de la Chanvrerie, he owed his life to magnanimity of insurgent who, holding him under pistol, fired into air instead of blowing out his brains. **Marius possessed evidence, certain date, irrefragable proof. "You are an infamous wretch! you are a liar, a calumniator, a villain... you have only succeeded in glorifying him. And it is you who are the thief! And it is you who are the assassin! I saw you, Thénardier Jondrette, in that lair on the Rue de l'Hôpital."** Offered twenty thousand francs total, ordered him to America with daughter; wife dead. **The moral wretchedness of Thénardier was irremediable. He was in America what he had been in Europe. With Marius' money, Thénardier set up as slave-dealer.**
